lesson_scope: Resolving coplanar forces along orthogonal axes, Cartesian sign conventions, inclined plane weight and applied force resolution, exact trigonometric ratios, and critical normal reaction boundary conditions.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: direct resolution of a single force along the adjacent horizontal axis.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Direct application of F_x = F*cos(theta).

hints: The component of a force $F$ adjacent to the angle $\theta$ is given by $F_x = F\cos\theta$.
Calculate $50\cos 35^\circ$ on your calculator and round your answer to 3 significant figures.

walkthrough.text:
Resolve the force along the positive $x$-axis:
$$F_x = F\cos\theta = 50\cos 35^\circ$$

Evaluate the trigonometric product:
$$F_x = 50 \times 0.819152 = 40.9576\text{ N} \approx 41.0\text{ N}$$
To 3 significant figures, $F_x = 41.0\text{ N}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Applies $F_x = F\cos\theta$ by forming $50\cos 35^\circ$.
Evaluates to $41.0\text{ N}$ correct to 3 significant figures.

teacher_walkthrough.text:
We want the horizontal effect of this diagonal pull:
- Force magnitude: $F = 50\text{ N}$
- Angle with horizontal ($x$-axis): $\theta = 35^\circ$
Because the horizontal component is adjacent to the angle, use cosine:
$$F_x = F\cos\theta$$

Substitute the given numbers and calculate:
$$F_x = 50\cos 35^\circ$$
Evaluate the cosine:
$$\cos 35^\circ \approx 0.819152$$
$$F_x = 50 \times 0.819152 = 40.9576\text{ N}$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $41.0\text{ N}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: resolving a force when the angle is specified relative to the vertical axis.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Handling angle measured from vertical: F_x = F*sin(theta).

hints: When the angle $\theta$ is given with the vertical axis, the horizontal component is opposite the angle, so use $F_x = F\sin\theta$ (or $F\cos(90^\circ - \theta)$).
Compute $40\sin 25^\circ$ and round to 3 significant figures.

walkthrough.text:
Resolve the force horizontally using the angle with the vertical:
$$F_x = F\sin\theta = 40\sin 25^\circ$$
(or $F_x = 40\cos(90^\circ - 25^\circ) = 40\cos 65^\circ$)

Evaluate the horizontal component:
$$F_x = 40 \times 0.422618 = 16.9047\text{ N} \approx 16.9\text{ N}$$
To 3 significant figures, $F_x = 16.9\text{ N}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Forms $40\sin 25^\circ$ or $40\cos(90^\circ - 25^\circ)$ for horizontal component.
Evaluates to $16.9\text{ N}$ correct to 3 significant figures.

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Check where the angle is measured:
- The angle $25^\circ$ is given with the vertical axis, not the ground.
- In the resolution triangle, the horizontal leg is opposite this $25^\circ$ angle.
Therefore, the horizontal component uses sine:
$$F_x = F\sin 25^\circ$$
(Alternatively, the angle with the ground is $90^\circ - 25^\circ = 65^\circ$, so $F_x = 40\cos 65^\circ$.)

Now compute the horizontal value:
$$F_x = 40\sin 25^\circ$$
Evaluate the sine:
$$\sin 25^\circ \approx 0.422618$$
$$F_x = 40 \times 0.422618 = 16.9047\text{ N}$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $16.9\text{ N}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: applying Cartesian sign convention for forces pointing in negative coordinate directions.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Negative sign convention in Cartesian components.

hints: A force pointing into the second quadrant has a negative $x$-component because it acts in the direction of negative $x$.
Calculate $-65\cos 40^\circ$ and state the value to 3 significant figures.

walkthrough.text:
Identify the Cartesian direction and resolve along the negative $x$-axis:
$$F_x = -F\cos\theta = -65\cos 40^\circ$$
(or $F_x = 65\cos 140^\circ$)

Evaluate the component with sign:
$$F_x = -65 \times 0.766044 = -49.7929\text{ N} \approx -49.8\text{ N}$$
To 3 significant figures, $F_x = -49.8\text{ N}$ (or $49.8\text{ N}$ to the left).

ai_rubric.observable: Identifies negative direction along $x$-axis and forms $-65\cos 40^\circ$ or $65\cos 140^\circ$.
Obtains $-49.8\text{ N}$ (or states $49.8\text{ N}$ in negative $x$-direction).

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Check the direction along the $x$-axis:
- Positive $x$ points to the right.
- This force points into the second quadrant, pulling to the left.
Because it pulls to the left, its $x$-component is negative:
$$F_x = -F\cos\theta = -65\cos 40^\circ$$
(Or using standard angle $180^\circ - 40^\circ = 140^\circ$: $F_x = 65\cos 140^\circ$.)

Calculate the numerical value:
$$\cos 40^\circ \approx 0.766044$$
$$F_x = -65 \times 0.766044 = -49.7929\text{ N}$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $-49.8\text{ N}$ (or $49.8\text{ N}$ to the left).

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: resolving the weight of an object parallel to an inclined slope.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Weight resolution on inclined plane: W_parallel = mg*sin(alpha).

hints: The weight of the object is $W = mg$. The component of gravity pulling down an incline of angle $\alpha$ is $W_\parallel = mg\sin\alpha$.
Substitute $m = 6\text{ kg}$, $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, and $\alpha = 30^\circ$ into $mg\sin 30^\circ$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate weight and resolve down the inclined plane:
$$W = mg = 6 \times 10 = 60\text{ N}$$
$$W_\parallel = W\sin\alpha = 60\sin 30^\circ$$

Evaluate using $\sin 30^\circ = 0.5$:
$$W_\parallel = 60 \times 0.5 = 30\text{ N}$$
The component of weight down the slope is $30\text{ N}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Applies $W_\parallel = mg\sin 30^\circ$ with $m = 6$ and $g = 10$.
Evaluates to exact value $30\text{ N}$.

teacher_walkthrough.text:
First calculate the weight of the block:
$$W = mg = 6 \times 10 = 60\text{ N}$$
On an inclined plane of angle $\alpha$, gravity splits into two standard parts:
- Down the slope (parallel): $W_\parallel = mg\sin\alpha$
- Into the slope (perpendicular): $W_\perp = mg\cos\alpha$
Here we want the component pulling down the slope, so we use sine:
$$W_\parallel = mg\sin 30^\circ$$

Substitute the values:
$$W_\parallel = 60\sin 30^\circ$$
Since $\sin 30^\circ = 0.5$ exactly:
$$W_\parallel = 60 \times 0.5 = 30\text{ N}$$
The downward component along the slope is exactly $30\text{ N}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: resolving forces using exact trigonometric ratios without finding intermediate angles.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Trigonometric ratio resolution with pythagorean triples.

hints: Use a $3-4-5$ right-angled triangle where $\text{opposite} = 3$ and $\text{adjacent} = 4$ to determine the exact value of $\sin\theta$.
Multiply the force magnitude $75\text{ N}$ by the exact fraction $\sin\theta = \frac{3}{5}$.

walkthrough.text:
Deduce exact trigonometric ratios from $\tan\theta = \frac{3}{4}$:
$$\text{Hypotenuse } = \sqrt{3^2 + 4^2} = 5 \implies \sin\theta = \frac{3}{5}, \quad \cos\theta = \frac{4}{5}$$

Calculate vertical component:
$$F_y = F\sin\theta = 75 \times \frac{3}{5} = 45\text{ N}$$
The exact vertical component is $45\text{ N}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Deduces $\sin\theta = \frac{3}{5}$ from $\tan\theta = \frac{3}{4}$ and multiplies by $75$.
Obtains exact vertical component $45\text{ N}$.

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Avoid decimals by using a right-angled reference triangle:
- Given $\tan\theta = \frac{3}{4}$, so opposite = 3 and adjacent = 4.
- Find the hypotenuse using Pythagoras:
$$h = \sqrt{3^2 + 4^2} = \sqrt{9 + 16} = 5$$
Now write down the exact sine ratio:
$$\sin\theta = \frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{hypotenuse}} = \frac{3}{5}$$

Calculate the vertical component directly:
$$F_y = F\sin\theta = 75 \times \frac{3}{5}$$
Simplify without decimals:
$$F_y = 15 \times 3 = 45\text{ N}$$
The exact vertical component is $45\text{ N}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: resolving a force perpendicular to an inclined plane.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Perpendicular resolution of pulling force on an incline: F_perp = F*sin(beta).

hints: The force makes an angle of $20^\circ$ with the surface of the incline. Its component perpendicular to the surface is $F_\perp = F\sin 20^\circ$.
Evaluate $80\sin 20^\circ$ and round your answer to 3 significant figures.

walkthrough.text:
Identify components aligned with and perpendicular to the inclined plane:
$$F_\parallel = 80\cos 20^\circ$$
$$F_\perp = 80\sin 20^\circ$$

Evaluate perpendicular component away from the surface:
$$F_\perp = 80\sin 20^\circ = 80 \times 0.342020 = 27.3616\text{ N} \approx 27.4\text{ N}$$
To 3 significant figures, $F_\perp = 27.4\text{ N}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Resolves perpendicular to plane by forming $80\sin 20^\circ$.
Evaluates to $27.4\text{ N}$ correct to 3 significant figures.

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Look at the pulling force relative to the slope:
- Force magnitude: $F = 80\text{ N}$
- Angle above the surface of the slope: $\beta = 20^\circ$
Resolving relative to the plane:
$$F_\parallel = F\cos 20^\circ \quad (\text{up the plane})$$
$$F_\perp = F\sin 20^\circ \quad (\text{perpendicular to the plane})$$

Calculate the perpendicular component:
$$F_\perp = 80\sin 20^\circ$$
Evaluate the sine:
$$\sin 20^\circ \approx 0.342020$$
$$F_\perp = 80 \times 0.342020 = 27.3616\text{ N}$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $27.4\text{ N}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Core Practice Easy: resolving two coplanar forces along horizontal and vertical axes.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Summing horizontal components of coplanar forces at an angle.

hints: Sum the horizontal contributions of both forces: the $20\text{ N}$ force acts entirely along the positive $x$-axis, while the $30\text{ N}$ force contributes $30\cos 60^\circ$.
Evaluate $20 + 30\cos 60^\circ$ using $\cos 60^\circ = 0.5$.

walkthrough.text:
Resolve both coplanar forces along the positive $x$-axis:
$$X = 20\cos 0^\circ + 30\cos 60^\circ = 20 + 30\cos 60^\circ$$

Evaluate using $\cos 60^\circ = 0.5$:
$$X = 20 + 30(0.5) = 20 + 15 = 35\text{ N}$$
The net component in the positive $x$-direction is $35\text{ N}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Sums horizontal components by setting up $20 + 30\cos 60^\circ$.
Evaluates to exact value $35\text{ N}$.

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Sum the horizontal contributions of both forces ($X = \Sigma F_x$):
- The $20\text{ N}$ force acts entirely along $+x$: $+20\text{ N}$
- The $30\text{ N}$ force acts at $60^\circ$ above $+x$: $+30\cos 60^\circ$
Set up the horizontal sum:
$$X = 20 + 30\cos 60^\circ$$

Use the exact value $\cos 60^\circ = 0.5$:
$$X = 20 + 30(0.5)$$
$$X = 20 + 15 = 35\text{ N}$$
The net component in the positive $x$-direction is $35\text{ N}$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Summing vertical components of coplanar forces.

hints: The $20\text{ N}$ force is purely horizontal and has zero vertical component. The $30\text{ N}$ force contributes $30\sin 60^\circ$.
Use the exact trigonometric value $\sin 60^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ to express the result in surd form and compute its 3-significant-figure value.

walkthrough.text:
Resolve both coplanar forces along the positive $y$-axis:
$$Y = 20\sin 0^\circ + 30\sin 60^\circ = 0 + 30\sin 60^\circ$$

Evaluate using exact surd $\sin 60^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$:
$$Y = 30 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = 15\sqrt{3}\text{ N} \approx 26.0\text{ N}$$
The vertical component is $15\sqrt{3}\text{ N}$ (or $26.0\text{ N}$ to 3 significant figures).

ai_rubric.observable: Sets up vertical resolution $30\sin 60^\circ$.
Obtains $15\sqrt{3}\text{ N}$ or $26.0\text{ N}$ to 3 significant figures.

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Sum the vertical contributions of both forces ($Y = \Sigma F_y$):
- The $20\text{ N}$ force is horizontal, so its vertical contribution is $0\text{ N}$.
- The $30\text{ N}$ force pulls upwards, contributing $+30\sin 60^\circ$.
Set up the vertical sum:
$$Y = 0 + 30\sin 60^\circ$$

Use the exact surd value $\sin 60^\circ = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$:
$$Y = 30 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = 15\sqrt{3}\text{ N}$$
In decimal form:
$$15\sqrt{3} \approx 15 \times 1.73205 = 25.9808\text{ N} \approx 26.0\text{ N}$$
Both $15\sqrt{3}\text{ N}$ and $26.0\text{ N}$ are accepted.

questions.difficulty_reason: Core Practice Easy: resolving an angled pulling force and finding normal reaction force.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Horizontal resolution of an angled tension force.

hints: The rope pulls with tension $50\text{ N}$ at $28^\circ$ to the horizontal. Its horizontal component is $T_x = T\cos 28^\circ$.
Calculate $50\cos 28^\circ$ and round your answer to 3 significant figures.

walkthrough.text:
Resolve the rope tension along the horizontal floor:
$$T_x = T\cos 28^\circ = 50\cos 28^\circ$$

Evaluate to 3 significant figures:
$$T_x = 50 \times 0.882948 = 44.1474\text{ N} \approx 44.1\text{ N}$$
The forward horizontal force is $44.1\text{ N}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Resolves tension horizontally by forming $50\cos 28^\circ$.
Evaluates to $44.1\text{ N}$ correct to 3 significant figures.

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Find the forward pulling force along the floor:
- Rope tension: $T = 50\text{ N}$
- Angle above horizontal floor: $\theta = 28^\circ$
The component adjacent to the floor is:
$$T_x = T\cos 28^\circ$$

Calculate the value:
$$T_x = 50\cos 28^\circ$$
$$\cos 28^\circ \approx 0.882948$$
$$T_x = 50 \times 0.882948 = 44.1474\text{ N}$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $44.1\text{ N}$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Vertical force balance with upward tension component reducing normal reaction.

hints: The upward component of tension $T\sin 28^\circ$ acts alongside the normal contact force $R$ to support the weight $mg$. Set up $R + T\sin 28^\circ = mg$.
Calculate $mg = 8 \times 10 = 80\text{ N}$ and subtract $50\sin 28^\circ$ to find $R$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the upward vertical component of tension:
$$T_y = 50\sin 28^\circ = 50 \times 0.469472 = 23.4736\text{ N}$$

Set up vertical equilibrium $R + T_y = mg$ and solve for normal contact force $R$:
$$R + 23.4736 = 8 \times 10 = 80$$
$$R = 80 - 23.4736 = 56.5264\text{ N} \approx 56.5\text{ N}$$
To 3 significant figures, $R = 56.5\text{ N}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Calculates vertical component of tension as $50\sin 28^\circ$ ($23.47\text{ N}$).
Sets up vertical equilibrium $R + 50\sin 28^\circ = 8 \times 10$.
Solves for normal reaction to obtain $56.5\text{ N}$.

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Calculate the upward lift from the rope:
$$T_y = T\sin 28^\circ = 50\sin 28^\circ$$
$$\sin 28^\circ \approx 0.469472 \implies T_y = 50 \times 0.469472 = 23.4736\text{ N}$$
Because the rope pulls upwards, it helps support the box and reduces the floor contact force.

Balance vertical forces (normal contact force $R$ + upward tension = weight):
$$R + T_y = mg$$
Substitute $mg = 8 \times 10 = 80\text{ N}$:
$$R + 23.4736 = 80$$
$$R = 80 - 23.4736 = 56.5264\text{ N}$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $R = 56.5\text{ N}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Core Practice Medium: resolving three multi-quadrant coplanar forces along Cartesian axes.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Multi-force resolution along x-axis with acute and third-quadrant angles.

hints: Identify the horizontal contribution of each force: the $15\text{ N}$ force acts along $+x$, the $25\text{ N}$ force contributes in $+x$, and the $20\text{ N}$ force points towards $-x$.
Write the algebraic sum of horizontal components: $X = 15 + 25\cos 40^\circ - 20\cos 70^\circ$.
Evaluate the trigonometric values: $\cos 40^\circ \approx 0.7660$ and $\cos 70^\circ \approx 0.3420$, then compute the final sum to 3 significant figures.

walkthrough.text:
Sum the horizontal components of all three coplanar forces:
$$X = 15 + 25\cos 40^\circ - 20\cos 70^\circ$$

Evaluate the terms:
$$X = 15 + 25(0.766044) - 20(0.342020) = 15 + 19.1511 - 6.8404 = 27.3107\text{ N} \approx 27.3\text{ N}$$
To 3 significant figures, $X = 27.3\text{ N}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Resolves all forces horizontally using cosines: $15$, $25\cos 40^\circ$, and $20\cos 70^\circ$.
Assigns correct signs: $X = 15 + 25\cos 40^\circ - 20\cos 70^\circ$.
Evaluates to $27.3\text{ N}$ correct to 3 significant figures.

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Break down the horizontal component of each force:
- $15\text{ N}$ force: acts purely along $+x \implies +15\text{ N}$
- $25\text{ N}$ force: acts into quadrant 1 $\implies +25\cos 40^\circ$
- $20\text{ N}$ force: acts into quadrant 3 (to the left) $\implies -20\cos 70^\circ$
Assemble the horizontal sum:
$$X = 15 + 25\cos 40^\circ - 20\cos 70^\circ$$

Evaluate the terms:
$$25\cos 40^\circ \approx 25 \times 0.766044 = 19.1511\text{ N}$$
$$20\cos 70^\circ \approx 20 \times 0.342020 = 6.8404\text{ N}$$
$$X = 15 + 19.1511 - 6.8404 = 27.3107\text{ N}$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $27.3\text{ N}$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Multi-force resolution along y-axis with opposite vertical directions.

hints: The $15\text{ N}$ force acts along the horizontal axis, so its vertical contribution is zero.
The $25\text{ N}$ force has an upward component $+25\sin 40^\circ$, while the $20\text{ N}$ force points downward with component $-20\sin 70^\circ$.
Calculate $Y = 25\sin 40^\circ - 20\sin 70^\circ$ and evaluate the result to 3 significant figures.

walkthrough.text:
Sum the vertical components of all three coplanar forces:
$$Y = 0 + 25\sin 40^\circ - 20\sin 70^\circ$$

Evaluate the terms:
$$Y = 25(0.642788) - 20(0.939693) = 16.0697 - 18.7939 = -2.7242\text{ N} \approx -2.72\text{ N}$$
To 3 significant figures, $Y = -2.72\text{ N}$ (or $2.72\text{ N}$ in the negative $y$-direction).

ai_rubric.observable: Sets up vertical resolution $Y = 25\sin 40^\circ - 20\sin 70^\circ$.
Evaluates to $-2.72\text{ N}$ (or $2.72\text{ N}$ in negative $y$-direction).

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Break down the vertical component of each force:
- $15\text{ N}$ force: horizontal, so $0\text{ N}$
- $25\text{ N}$ force: pulls upwards $\implies +25\sin 40^\circ$
- $20\text{ N}$ force: pulls downwards $\implies -20\sin 70^\circ$
Assemble the vertical sum:
$$Y = 25\sin 40^\circ - 20\sin 70^\circ$$

Evaluate the terms:
$$25\sin 40^\circ \approx 25 \times 0.642788 = 16.0697\text{ N}$$
$$20\sin 70^\circ \approx 20 \times 0.939693 = 18.7939\text{ N}$$
$$Y = 16.0697 - 18.7939 = -2.7242\text{ N}$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $-2.72\text{ N}$ (or $2.72\text{ N}$ downwards).

questions.difficulty_reason: Core Practice Medium: resolving horizontal applied force and weight on an inclined slope using exact Pythagorean ratios.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Trigonometric deduction from tan(alpha) and weight resolution down an incline.

hints: Find the hypotenuse using the Pythagorean theorem: $\sqrt{7^2 + 24^2} = 25$, then state $\sin\alpha$ and $\cos\alpha$.
The component of the weight acting parallel to the slope down the plane is $mg\sin\alpha$.
Multiply $mg = 5 \times 10 = 50\text{ N}$ by $\sin\alpha = \frac{7}{25}$ to evaluate the parallel weight component.

walkthrough.text:
Find exact trigonometric ratios from $\tan\alpha = \frac{7}{24}$:
$$\text{Hypotenuse } = \sqrt{7^2 + 24^2} = \sqrt{49 + 576} = \sqrt{625} = 25$$
$$\sin\alpha = \frac{7}{25}, \quad \cos\alpha = \frac{24}{25}$$

Calculate component of weight down the plane:
$$W_\parallel = mg\sin\alpha = (5 \times 10) \times \frac{7}{25} = 50 \times \frac{7}{25} = 14\text{ N}$$
The component of weight acting down the plane is $14\text{ N}$.

ai_rubric.observable: States or calculates $\sin\alpha = \frac{7}{25}$ and $\cos\alpha = \frac{24}{25}$.
Calculates weight component down slope as $50 \times \frac{7}{25} = 14\text{ N}$.

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Use the $(7, 24, 25)$ right-angled triangle from $\tan\alpha = \frac{7}{24}$:
$$\text{Hypotenuse} = \sqrt{7^2 + 24^2} = 25$$
Write the exact sine and cosine ratios:
$$\sin\alpha = \frac{7}{25}, \quad \cos\alpha = \frac{24}{25}$$

Find the weight component down the slope:
- Block weight: $W = mg = 5 \times 10 = 50\text{ N}$
- Component parallel to slope:
$$W_\parallel = mg\sin\alpha = 50 \times \frac{7}{25}$$
$$W_\parallel = 2 \times 7 = 14\text{ N}$$
The weight component pulling down the slope is exactly $14\text{ N}$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Combined perpendicular resolution of weight and horizontal pushing force on an incline.

hints: Both the weight and the horizontal pushing force press perpendicularly into the inclined plane.
The perpendicular component of the weight is $mg\cos\alpha$, and the perpendicular component of the $30\text{ N}$ horizontal force is $30\sin\alpha$.
Substitute $\cos\alpha = \frac{24}{25}$ and $\sin\alpha = \frac{7}{25}$ into $mg\cos\alpha + 30\sin\alpha$.

walkthrough.text:
Resolve weight and horizontal pushing force perpendicular to the plane:
$$W_\perp = mg\cos\alpha = 50 \times \frac{24}{25} = 48\text{ N}$$
$$F_\perp = 30\sin\alpha = 30 \times \frac{7}{25} = 8.4\text{ N}$$

Sum the perpendicular components pressing into the plane:
$$\text{Total Perpendicular Force} = W_\perp + F_\perp = 48 + 8.4 = 56.4\text{ N}$$
The total component acting perpendicular to the inclined plane is $56.4\text{ N}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Resolves weight perpendicular to plane: $50\cos\alpha = 50 \times \frac{24}{25} = 48\text{ N}$.
Resolves horizontal pushing force perpendicular to plane: $30\sin\alpha = 30 \times \frac{7}{25} = 8.4\text{ N}$.
Sums perpendicular components to obtain $48 + 8.4 = 56.4\text{ N}$.

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Identify all forces pressing into the plane:
1. Weight component into the slope:
$$W_\perp = mg\cos\alpha = 50 \times \frac{24}{25} = 48\text{ N}$$
2. Horizontal $30\text{ N}$ push into the slope:
$$F_\perp = 30\sin\alpha = 30 \times \frac{7}{25} = 8.4\text{ N}$$

Add both perpendicular components together:
$$\text{Total Perpendicular Force} = W_\perp + F_\perp$$
$$\text{Total Perpendicular Force} = 48 + 8.4 = 56.4\text{ N}$$
The total perpendicular force pressing into the plane is $56.4\text{ N}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Core Practice Medium: recovering unknown magnitude and angle from known orthogonal resolved components.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Algebraic isolation of P*cos(theta) and P*sin(theta) to deduce angle.

hints: Set up equations for the total $x$-component and total $y$-component: $P\cos\theta - 24 = 12$ and $P\sin\theta + 10 = 28$.
Isolate $P\cos\theta$ and $P\sin\theta$ by rearranging both linear equations.
Divide the expression for $P\sin\theta$ by $P\cos\theta$ to cancel $P$ and find $\tan\theta$, then compute $\arctan(0.5)$.

walkthrough.text:
Set up resolution equations along the $x$ and $y$ axes:
$$P\cos\theta - 24 = 12 \implies P\cos\theta = 36$$
$$P\sin\theta + 10 = 28 \implies P\sin\theta = 18$$

Divide to eliminate $P$ and find $\theta$:
$$\tan\theta = \frac{P\sin\theta}{P\cos\theta} = \frac{18}{36} = 0.5$$
$$\theta = \arctan(0.5) \approx 26.5651^\circ \approx 26.6^\circ$$
To 1 decimal place, $\theta = 26.6^\circ$.

ai_rubric.observable: Sets up $P\cos\theta - 24 = 12$ and $P\sin\theta + 10 = 28$.
Solves for $P\cos\theta = 36$ and $P\sin\theta = 18$, and divides to show $\tan\theta = 0.5$.
Evaluates $\theta = \arctan(0.5) = 26.6^\circ$ correct to 1 decimal place.

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Write down the equations for net horizontal and net vertical forces:
- Horizontal: $P\cos\theta$ rightwards, $24\text{ N}$ leftwards, net is $12\text{ N}$:
$$P\cos\theta - 24 = 12 \implies P\cos\theta = 36$$
- Vertical: $P\sin\theta$ upwards, $10\text{ N}$ upwards, net is $28\text{ N}$:
$$P\sin\theta + 10 = 28 \implies P\sin\theta = 18$$

Divide the two equations to eliminate $P$ and find $\theta$:
$$\frac{P\sin\theta}{P\cos\theta} = \frac{18}{36} \implies \tan\theta = 0.5$$
Now compute the angle:
$$\theta = \arctan(0.5) \approx 26.5651^\circ$$
Rounding to 1 decimal place gives $\theta = 26.6^\circ$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Pythagorean recovery of force magnitude from orthogonal components.

hints: Use the Pythagorean relationship $(P\cos\theta)^2 + (P\sin\theta)^2 = P^2(\cos^2\theta + \sin^2\theta) = P^2$.
Simplify $\sqrt{1620}$ by factoring out the largest perfect square ($324 \times 5$), then find the decimal equivalent to 3 significant figures.

walkthrough.text:
Square and add the isolated components:
$$P^2 = (P\cos\theta)^2 + (P\sin\theta)^2 = 36^2 + 18^2 = 1296 + 324 = 1620$$

Simplify the square root and evaluate:
$$P = \sqrt{1620} = \sqrt{324 \times 5} = 18\sqrt{5}\text{ N} \approx 40.2\text{ N}$$
The exact magnitude is $18\sqrt{5}\text{ N}$, and to 3 significant figures it is $40.2\text{ N}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Squares and adds components: $P^2 = 36^2 + 18^2$.
Simplifies $\sqrt{1620}$ to exact surd $18\sqrt{5}\text{ N}$.
Evaluates to $40.2\text{ N}$ correct to 3 significant figures.

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Find $P$ exactly using $\cos^2\theta + \sin^2\theta = 1$:
$$(P\cos\theta)^2 + (P\sin\theta)^2 = P^2$$
Substitute $P\cos\theta = 36$ and $P\sin\theta = 18$:
$$P^2 = 36^2 + 18^2 = 1296 + 324 = 1620$$

Take the square root and simplify the surd:
$$P = \sqrt{1620} = \sqrt{324 \times 5} = 18\sqrt{5}\text{ N}$$
In decimal form:
$$18\sqrt{5} \approx 18 \times 2.236068 = 40.2492\text{ N} \approx 40.2\text{ N}$$
The exact magnitude is $18\sqrt{5}\text{ N}$, and to 3 s.f. it is $40.2\text{ N}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Core Practice Hard: multi-force exact surd resolution and resolution along a rotated reference axis.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Exact surd evaluation of multiple coplanar forces along Cartesian axes.

hints: Find the horizontal component of each force separately using exact values for $\cos 45^\circ$ and $\cos 30^\circ$.
For $F_2$, note that $10\sqrt{2}\cos 45^\circ = 10\sqrt{2}\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right) = 10\text{ N}$.
For $F_3$, the force acts in the second quadrant, so its horizontal component is negative: $-20\cos 30^\circ = -20\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) = -10\sqrt{3}\text{ N}$.
Add all three horizontal components together to obtain the exact expression in the form $a - b\sqrt{3}$.

walkthrough.text:
Decompose each force along the positive $x$-axis using exact trigonometric values:
$$F_{1x} = 20\cos 0^\circ = 20\text{ N}$$
$$F_{2x} = 10\sqrt{2}\cos 45^\circ = 10\sqrt{2} \times \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} = 10\text{ N}$$
$$F_{3x} = -20\cos 30^\circ = -20 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = -10\sqrt{3}\text{ N}$$

Sum the horizontal components:
$$X = 20 + 10 - 10\sqrt{3} = 30 - 10\sqrt{3}\text{ N}$$
The exact net component in the $x$-direction is $30 - 10\sqrt{3}\text{ N}$.

ai_rubric.observable: States horizontal component of $F_1$ as $20\text{ N}$ and calculates $F_2$ horizontal component as $10\sqrt{2}\cos 45^\circ = 10\text{ N}$.
Resolves $F_3$ along $x$-axis using $-20\cos 30^\circ$.
Obtains $-10\sqrt{3}\text{ N}$ for the $x$-component of $F_3$.
Sums all three horizontal components to obtain exact value $30 - 10\sqrt{3}\text{ N}$.

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Resolve each force along the positive $x$-axis using exact values:
- $F_1 = 20\text{ N}$ along $+x \implies F_{1x} = +20\text{ N}$
- $F_2 = 10\sqrt{2}\text{ N}$ at $45^\circ$:
$$F_{2x} = 10\sqrt{2}\cos 45^\circ = 10\sqrt{2} \times \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = 10\text{ N}$$
- $F_3 = 20\text{ N}$ at $30^\circ$ above $-x$ (second quadrant):
$$F_{3x} = -20\cos 30^\circ = -20 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = -10\sqrt{3}\text{ N}$$

Add all three horizontal components together:
$$X = F_{1x} + F_{2x} + F_{3x}$$
$$X = 20 + 10 - 10\sqrt{3} = 30 - 10\sqrt{3}\text{ N}$$
The exact net component in the $x$-direction is $30 - 10\sqrt{3}\text{ N}$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Projecting Cartesian components onto an arbitrary non-standard inclined axis.

hints: A resultant with orthogonal components $(X, Y)$ has resolved component $U = X\cos\alpha + Y\sin\alpha$ along an axis inclined at angle $\alpha$ to the $x$-axis.
Calculate the total vertical component $Y$: $F_{1y} = 0$, $F_{2y} = 10\sqrt{2}\sin 45^\circ = 10$, and $F_{3y} = 20\sin 30^\circ = 10$, giving $Y = 20\text{ N}$.
Substitute $X = 30 - 10\sqrt{3}$ and $Y = 20$ into $U = X\cos 30^\circ + Y\sin 30^\circ$ with $\alpha = 30^\circ$.
Expand $(30 - 10\sqrt{3})\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) + 20\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) = 15\sqrt{3} - 15 + 10$ and simplify.

walkthrough.text:
Find the total vertical component $Y$:
$$Y = 0 + 10\sqrt{2}\sin 45^\circ + 20\sin 30^\circ = 10 + 20(0.5) = 20\text{ N}$$

Resolve along the $u$-axis rotated by $30^\circ$:
$$U = X\cos 30^\circ + Y\sin 30^\circ = (30 - 10\sqrt{3})\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) + 20\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)$$
$$U = 15\sqrt{3} - 15 + 10 = 15\sqrt{3} - 5\text{ N}$$
The exact total resolved component along the $u$-axis is $15\sqrt{3} - 5\text{ N}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Finds total vertical component $Y = 10\sqrt{2}\sin 45^\circ + 20\sin 30^\circ = 20\text{ N}$ (or identifies angles to $u$-axis: $30^\circ$, $15^\circ$, $120^\circ$).
Applies rotated resolution $U = X\cos 30^\circ + Y\sin 30^\circ$ (or sums $\Sigma F_i \cos\theta_i$).
Simplifies exactly to obtain $15\sqrt{3} - 5\text{ N}$.

teacher_walkthrough.text:
First find the total vertical component $Y$:
- $F_{1y} = 0\text{ N}$
- $F_{2y} = 10\sqrt{2}\sin 45^\circ = 10\text{ N}$
- $F_{3y} = 20\sin 30^\circ = 20(0.5) = 10\text{ N}$
$$Y = 0 + 10 + 10 = 20\text{ N}$$

Project the net force $(X, Y)$ onto the $u$-axis inclined at $30^\circ$:
$$U = X\cos 30^\circ + Y\sin 30^\circ$$
Substitute $X = 30 - 10\sqrt{3}$ and $Y = 20$:
$$U = (30 - 10\sqrt{3})\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right) + 20\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)$$
$$U = 15\sqrt{3} - 15 + 10 = 15\sqrt{3} - 5\text{ N}$$
The exact resolved component along the $u$-axis is $15\sqrt{3} - 5\text{ N}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Core Practice Hard (Capstone): comprehensive synthesis of inclined plane resolution, zero-net-force tension equilibrium, normal contact force, and critical lift-off acceleration.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Parallel resolution with pulling force at angle to the slope.

hints: Resolve forces parallel to the inclined plane: weight acts down the slope with component $mg\sin 25^\circ$, and the pulling force acts up the slope with component $T\cos 15^\circ$.
For zero net force along the incline, equate the upward and downward components: $T\cos 15^\circ = mg\sin 25^\circ$.
Substitute $m = 12\text{ kg}$ and $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$ to get $120\sin 25^\circ \approx 50.714\text{ N}$.
Divide $50.714$ by $\cos 15^\circ \approx 0.96593$ and round your answer to 3 significant figures.

walkthrough.text:
Express components parallel to the inclined slope:
$$W_\parallel = mg\sin 25^\circ = 120\sin 25^\circ$$
$$T_\parallel = T\cos 15^\circ$$

Equate components for equilibrium along the incline:
$$T\cos 15^\circ = 120\sin 25^\circ$$
$$T = \frac{120\sin 25^\circ}{\cos 15^\circ} = \frac{50.7142}{0.965926} = 52.5032\text{ N} \approx 52.5\text{ N}$$
To 3 significant figures, $T = 52.5\text{ N}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Expresses parallel components: $W_\parallel = 120\sin 25^\circ$ down the slope and $T_\parallel = T\cos 15^\circ$ up the slope.
Equates parallel components: $T\cos 15^\circ = 120\sin 25^\circ$.
Solves for $T$ to obtain $52.5\text{ N}$ correct to 3 significant figures.

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Identify the components parallel to the slope:
- Gravity pulling down the slope:
$$W_\parallel = mg\sin 25^\circ = 120\sin 25^\circ$$
- Tension pulling up the slope:
$$T_\parallel = T\cos 15^\circ$$

Equate the components for equilibrium along the incline:
$$T\cos 15^\circ = 120\sin 25^\circ$$
Evaluate the trigonometric values:
$$120\sin 25^\circ \approx 50.7142\text{ N}, \quad \cos 15^\circ \approx 0.965926$$
$$T = \frac{50.7142}{0.965926} = 52.5032\text{ N}$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $T = 52.5\text{ N}$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Perpendicular resolution on incline with outward normal contact force.

hints: Identify all forces acting perpendicular to the inclined slope: the normal contact force $R$ acts outwards, the pulling force has outward component $T\sin 15^\circ$, and weight has inward component $mg\cos 25^\circ$.
Set up the perpendicular force balance: $R + T\sin 15^\circ = mg\cos 25^\circ$.
Compute $120\cos 25^\circ \approx 108.76\text{ N}$ and $52.50\sin 15^\circ \approx 13.59\text{ N}$.
Subtract the tension component from the weight component to find $R$.

walkthrough.text:
Set up force balance perpendicular to the inclined slope:
$$R + T\sin 15^\circ = mg\cos 25^\circ = 120\cos 25^\circ$$

Substitute $T = 52.5032\text{ N}$ and solve for normal contact force $R$:
$$R = 120\cos 25^\circ - 52.5032\sin 15^\circ = 108.7570 - 13.5888 = 95.1682\text{ N} \approx 95.2\text{ N}$$
To 3 significant figures, $R = 95.2\text{ N}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Resolves perpendicular to slope: $R + T\sin 15^\circ = 120\cos 25^\circ$.
Substitutes $T = 52.5\text{ N}$ to obtain $R = 95.2\text{ N}$ correct to 3 significant figures.

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Balance the forces perpendicular to the slope:
- Normal contact force $R$ acts outward.
- Tension component $T\sin 15^\circ$ also acts outward.
- Weight component $120\cos 25^\circ$ acts inward.
$$R + T\sin 15^\circ = 120\cos 25^\circ$$

Substitute $T = 52.5032\text{ N}$ and solve for $R$:
$$120\cos 25^\circ \approx 108.7570\text{ N}$$
$$T\sin 15^\circ = 52.5032\sin 15^\circ \approx 13.5888\text{ N}$$
$$R = 108.7570 - 13.5888 = 95.1682\text{ N}$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $R = 95.2\text{ N}$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Critical boundary condition R = 0 on inclined plane and resultant Newton second law acceleration.

hints: The sledge is on the point of lifting off the inclined slope when the normal contact force drops to zero: $R = 0$.
Set $R = 0$ in the perpendicular resolution equation to obtain $T\sin 15^\circ = mg\cos 25^\circ$.
Solve for the critical tension: $T = \frac{120\cos 25^\circ}{\sin 15^\circ}$.
Determine the net force acting parallel to the slope up the incline: $F_\parallel = T\cos 15^\circ - mg\sin 25^\circ$.
Apply Newton's second law along the slope $F_\parallel = ma$ with $m = 12\text{ kg}$ to calculate the acceleration.

walkthrough.text:
Set normal contact force $R = 0$ in perpendicular equation to find lift-off tension:
$$0 + T\sin 15^\circ = 120\cos 25^\circ \implies T = \frac{120\cos 25^\circ}{\sin 15^\circ}$$
$$T = \frac{108.7570}{0.258819} = 420.2048\text{ N} \approx 420\text{ N}$$

Calculate net force parallel to slope and resulting acceleration:
$$F_\parallel = T\cos 15^\circ - 120\sin 25^\circ = 420.2048(0.965926) - 50.7142 = 355.1725\text{ N}$$
$$a = \frac{F_\parallel}{m} = \frac{355.1725}{12} = 29.5977\text{ m s}^{-2} \approx 29.6\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
To 3 significant figures, $T = 420\text{ N}$ and $a = 29.6\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Sets normal contact force $R = 0$ in the perpendicular equation to form $T\sin 15^\circ = 120\cos 25^\circ$.
Solves for critical tension to obtain $T = 420\text{ N}$.
Applies Newton's second law along the slope to obtain $a = 29.6\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Lift-off occurs when contact is lost, meaning $R = 0$:
$$0 + T\sin 15^\circ = 120\cos 25^\circ$$
$$T = \frac{120\cos 25^\circ}{\sin 15^\circ} = \frac{108.7570}{0.258819} = 420.2048\text{ N}$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives critical tension $T = 420\text{ N}$.

Calculate the resulting acceleration up the slope:
- Net force up the slope:
$$F_\parallel = T\cos 15^\circ - mg\sin 25^\circ$$
$$F_\parallel = 420.2048(0.965926) - 50.7142 = 405.8867 - 50.7142 = 355.1725\text{ N}$$
- Apply Newton's second law ($F = ma$ with $m = 12\text{ kg}$):
$$a = \frac{355.1725}{12} = 29.5977\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
Rounding to 3 significant figures gives $a = 29.6\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
